title: ci(test): run the shards when a markdown document a test READS changes
body:
Fixes #8861

## The blind spot

The `Decide whether this change needs a full run` step drops every markdown path before diffing, so a pull request whose files are all markdown leaves an empty diff and the test shards skip. That fast path is deliberate, the workflow says so in its own comment, and it is sound wherever a markdown change is inert.

It is not inert when a test **READS** the markdown file as data. The pull request then mutates a test's input while skipping the test that consumes it, and the page goes green on a question nobody asked. objectui#8857 measured the cost: one file changed, `packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md`, whose reader extracts the README's fences and evaluates them. `Test (shard 1/4)` reported success in ten seconds having run nothing; the merge-queue build then failed the same shard in 907 seconds and dequeued it. ⛔ The queue is not at fault and nothing here touches it.

## What this does — and what it deliberately does not

⛔ It does **not** make markdown-only pull requests run everything. That would discard the optimisation to fix a narrow class, and triage ruled it out by name. ⛔ No exclusion is removed or weakened; the pathspec list is byte-identical, and the three copies of it across this workflow still match, as their pin requires.

Instead the `test` job asks one more question of the markdown its exclusions dropped: **does a test read it?** `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs` answers, and the job runs in full only when the answer is yes.

Only the `test` job carries the extra stage. Measured: `type-check` reads no repository document, and no e2e spec does either (`docs-smoke.spec.ts` drives a running docs server and skips when there is none, which is the case in CI).

Failure posture matches the step's established one — a question that cannot be answered means RUN. Both new branches are spelled that way, and the pin that holds every `git diff` capture in this file to the fail-open form covers the new capture too.

## ⭐ The class is the deliverable — 21 and 27 were both ceilings

The card's **21** and the dispatch's re-measured **27** are co-occurrence counts (a test that calls `readFileSync(` and mentions `README.md`), and the card says so itself: *a ceiling on a heuristic, not a member count*. Neither is the class, and this pull request adopts neither. What ships is the derivation:

- **`ADJUDICATED`** — the answer a human gave for every candidate: what the test reads (`reads`), and which of the scanner's guesses it does **not** read (`notRead`), so a rejected candidate is recorded as rejected instead of vanishing.
- **`deriveCandidates()`** — the scanner, re-run from the tree on every audit. It masks comments through this repository's own `js-comment-mask`, reads string literals and comma-separated literal runs (the `join(ROOT, 'content', 'docs', …)` spelling), resolves each against the test's directory and every ancestor, and keeps only resolutions that exist. It also recognises a **directory walk**, which is how three of the real readers consume markdown without naming a single document.
- **`auditTree()`** — compares the two. A candidate nobody adjudicated is a finding, and so is a ledger row the tree no longer supports.

**What that derivation actually found: 45 candidate test files, 40 declared entries.** Asking each candidate *what it is* changed the answer in both directions:

- Three tests read a whole **tree** — `content/docs/**` (two of them) and `skills/objectui/**` — reading every document they find. A literal-only probe sees none of this, and it is most of the class by document count. `content/` holds nothing but `docs/`, so the `content/**` exclusion is effectively fully covered.
- Several candidates are **false positives** and are recorded as such: `create-plugin`'s `'README.md'` is a filename its generator *writes*, not a file in this tree; and a package-local `'README.md'` also resolves onto the root README through the ancestor walk. The root README is in the class anyway — two tests genuinely read it — but not for those tests' reasons.
- Two documents nobody would have guessed: `packages/components/README_SHADCN_SYNC.md` and `packages/vscode-extension/DESIGN.md`.

The derivation is what keeps this true as documents are added: a new test that reads markdown appears as an unadjudicated candidate and reds the audit, and a new page inside an already-declared tree is covered the moment it lands.

## ⭐ The firing control — both directions, and the negative leg

`scripts/__tests__/markdown-test-inputs.test.ts` extracts the step's real bytes from `ci.yml`, substitutes the event context, and runs them under `bash -e` against a real git repository whose pull request changes exactly the files under test.

| leg | input | step | `should_run` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **fires** | `packages/plugin-dashboard/README.md` | the widened `test` copy | **true**, naming the document |
| **before** | the same file | the `type-check` copy | **false** |
| **inert** | a newly added `packages/plugin-grid/NOTES.md` + a changeset | the widened `test` copy | **false** |
| **control** | `packages/plugin-grid/src/index.ts` | the widened `test` copy | **true** |

The *before* leg is not a reconstruction. This workflow carries three copies of the step; the `type-check` and `e2e` copies are untouched by this change and were byte-identical to the `test` copy before it, so "what it did before" is read out of the file rather than out of history.

The *inert* leg is what proves the trigger was widened rather than removed — a step that answered `true` unconditionally would pass every other row. Its document is added by the pull request, so it is inert by construction: nothing can read a file that did not exist.

**Ablation, on disk, measured.** With the widening reverted in `ci.yml` (the `test` job's step restored to the committed shape) and nothing else changed, the suite goes **4 failed | 8 passed** — including `FIRES … AssertionError: expected 'false' to be 'true'` on the objectui#8857 input, through the same evaluator. The *before*, *inert* and *control* legs stayed green, so the firing assertion is what carries the fix. The file was restored and verified byte-identical by hash.

The audit gets the same treatment: removing one ledger row takes `--audit` from exit 0 to exit 1 naming that reader, and two assertions plant synthetic candidates to prove the audit reports in both of its directions rather than passing an empty list.

## ⚠️ Stated limits — read before citing this as coverage

1. **`scripts/__tests__/**` is outside the scanned roots**, on triage's instruction. Measured while deriving this class, the reason given for that exclusion does not hold — it is about a pull request touching the *test*, while the hazard is a pull request touching the *markdown the test reads*, and those tests run in these same shards. That population reads `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `QUICK_REFERENCE.md`, `docs/**` and every package README. Filed as #9096 with the measurement, because taking it in would make nearly all repository markdown a test input, which is a different ruling.
2. **A read the scanner cannot see** — a path computed from parts no literal carries, or markdown read through a helper in another file — is invisible to it and therefore to the audit. No static scan closes that.
3. **Non-markdown inputs** are the same shape of hazard, but those paths are not excluded, so they already force a full run.

## Cost of the widening, measured

Over the last 86 first-parent commits on `main`: **7** would skip the shards under today's rule, and **2** of those now fire (a root README rewrite, and a `skills/objectui/guides/**` page). The other 5 — three changeset-only, one `AGENTS.md`, one `apps/site/**` — still skip. No commit in that window changed `content/docs/**` alone.

## Gates run

`scripts/__tests__` suite (140 files, 4151 tests) · the three `content/docs/**` tree readers · `check:doc-fences` · `check:control-bytes` · `check:entry-guard` · `check:unreferenced-sources` · `check:shell-escape-residue` · `check:skills-paths` · `check:new-line-citations` · `check-lint-coverage` · `check-doc-links` · `type-check:scripts` · `eslint --no-inline-config` on the new files — all green.

`check-changeset-presence` printed: *No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed* (4 files changed, 0 of them published source). No changeset in this pull request, and this repository has no `skip-changeset` label to apply.

`check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the four changed paths: **NOT GOVERNED** — an ordinary pull request.

The `ci-cd-pipeline.md` job table found the new command and demanded it be written down; that row now names it, which is the only reason this diff touches `content/`.
